segments.text: He lives through the atomic bomb at Hiroshima. Then he goes home. Home is Nagasaki.
No chance. Not both. Let's go look.
August {1945|nineteen forty-five}. Tsutomu Yamaguchi, an engineer, twenty-nine, is ending a work trip in Hiroshima. A flash. He is under two miles away.
Burned, eardrums burst, he shelters overnight. Next day, he goes home.
Three days on, bandaged, he is at work in Nagasaki, telling his boss about the bomb. His boss doesn't believe him.
Then the same white light fills the room. He lives again.
He lived to ninety-three. In {2009|two thousand nine}, Japan recognised him as a survivor of both. Officially, the only one.
He used those years to ask the world to give up the bomb. I was wrong. Case closed.
